newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Cambodia's Ranariddh to visit Jakarta.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Ranariddh to visit Jakarta.

text.p: Cambodia's overthrown First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh will arrive in Jakarta later on Wednesday, a foreign ministry official told Reuters.

The official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said Ranariddh would arrive on a commercial flight from Singapore. He said he had no details of the Cambodian leader's programme during the visit or whether he would meet President Suharto.
Ranariddh said in Singapore on Monday that he planned later in the week to visit Indonesia, which was one of the co-chairmen of the 1991 Paris talks which ended years of bloodshed in Cambodia.
The 1991 treaty laid the ground for United Nations-sponsored elections in Cambodia in 1993. Ranariddh won the poll and agreed to an uneasy power-sharing coalition with co-prime minister, Hun Sen.

Two weeks ago, the alliance crumbled and Hun Sen's troops drove Ranariddh's forces out of the capital Phnom Penh. Ranariddh, who was out of the country at the time, is seeking international support to force Hun Sen to agree to talks.
His visit comes as the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) holds a special ceremony in Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday to welcome new members Burma and Laos.
Cambodia was to have also joined, but ASEAN postponed its admission indefinitely following Hun Sen's overthrow of Ranariddh.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
